messages.content: New trip: I need to plan Atlanta for the arts evaluation convening, Jan. 27-29. Opening reception is late Wednesday afternoon, Thursday sessions are downtown, and Friday should wrap before lunch. I’d like flight-and-hotel pairings, no rental car if possible, and totals that are easy to defend.

I can compare that compactly. What airport should I start with from Chicago, and do you already have the event hotel block rate? Also, is Friday return timing more important than carrier if the plenary end time shifts a little?

Start with ORD. MDW only if it’s a real savings. The reception is 4:30 at the Hyatt Regency downtown. The block is $219 plus tax, and I don’t think breakfast is included. Friday end is listed as 11:30-ish. I’d like to return after lunch but not get home late.
Got it. One more fare assumption: regular economy or basic economy? And are you checking a bag?
Regular economy, carry-on only. United is fine if it’s comparable, but don’t force it if Delta is cleaner for Atlanta.

Here are the flight candidates I’d keep in play:

| Option | Wed ORD-ATL | Fri ATL-ORD | Est. fare | Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Delta | 10:05a-1:03p | 2:35p-3:42p | $258 | Best price/timing; plenty of reception buffer |
| United | 10:45a-1:43p | 2:25p-3:40p | $286 | Similar return, a little later inbound to ATL |
| American | 12:05p-3:05p | 4:20p-5:35p | $244 | Cheaper, but tight for 4:30 reception and later Friday |
Let’s keep Delta and United. Can I reasonably avoid a rental car from ATL to downtown?

Yes. MARTA is the budget choice: airport station to Peachtree Center in about 20-25 minutes, $2.50 each way, then a short walk to the Hyatt area. Rideshare is simpler with luggage, usually about 20-35 minutes depending on traffic and roughly $35-$45 each way. No rental car is needed for downtown sessions.
Now compare the hotel side: Hyatt block versus lower nearby hotels that include breakfast. I care about the two-night total, morning access, and room basics if they’re listed.

Hotel comparison for Jan. 27-29:

| Hotel | Est. 2-night lodging total | Breakfast | Room basics noted | Access/dinner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Hyatt Regency Atlanta block | about $512 with tax | not included | in-room coffee listed; mini-fridge should be confirmed/requested | event hotel; on-site restaurant/market; Peachtree Center nearby |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta-Downtown | about $372 with tax | included | coffee maker + mini-fridge listed | about 8-10 min walk or short rideshare to Hyatt; restaurants near Centennial/Peachtree |
| Residence Inn Atlanta Downtown | about $419 with tax | included | kitchenette/full fridge + coffee | about 10-12 min walk/MARTA-adjacent; fewer immediate dinner choices |
The Hampton savings look real. Is that walk okay for a January morning?

It’s workable if Thursday and Friday start at a normal conference time. The practical caveat is weather and darkness: an 8-10 minute downtown walk is fine in good conditions, but if the first session is early or rainy, you may end up using a short rideshare anyway. Still cheaper than the block, just less frictionless.
Can you pair the best flight choices with the hotels and show the trip total, excluding meals?

Estimated airfare + lodging + MARTA round trip:

| Pairing | Est. total | Timing | Key trade-off |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Delta + Hyatt block | about $775 | arrive 1:03 Wed; return 2:35 Fri | most convenient, no breakfast included |
| United + Hyatt block | about $803 | arrive 1:43 Wed; return 2:25 Fri | similar, slightly higher fare |
| Delta + Hampton | about $635 | same best flight timing | saves about $140, breakfast included, morning walk/short rideshare |
| United + Hampton | about $663 | strong return timing | still cheaper than block, slightly later Wed arrival |
What about Wednesday dinner if I don’t want to wander far after the reception?

Hyatt is easiest: on-site restaurant/bar and quick options around Peachtree Center. From Hampton, you’d have several downtown restaurants within a short walk, but after the reception you’d either walk back or take a quick rideshare. Residence Inn is fine for practical food, but less convenient for a post-reception dinner than staying at the Hyatt.
What would you hold today, before I know the exact Friday end time?

If the published agenda stays as-is, I’d hold the Hampton refundable room first: it saves meaningful money, includes breakfast, and still keeps you close enough without a car. I would not ticket flights until the Friday agenda is firmer; keep the Delta and United early-afternoon returns on the shortlist. Watch the Hyatt block deadline, because the recommendation changes if morning sessions move into the Hyatt early.
Good. For the Hampton hold, what should I ask them to confirm?

Ask for: refundable rate and exact cancellation deadline, one-bed room type, non-smoking quiet room, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, breakfast hours, itemized folio, and best walking route or rideshare drop-off for the Hyatt Regency. Also confirm whether the quoted rate has any destination or parking fee; you should not need parking, but it’s good to know.
If Friday really ends at 11:45, which return should I plan around?

Plan around the 2:25-2:35 p.m. return window. It gives enough time for a quick lunch or boxed lunch, MARTA/rideshare to ATL around 12:35-12:45, and still gets you back to Chicago before 4 p.m. Choose United at 2:25 if the fare stays close; choose Delta at 2:35 if it remains noticeably cheaper.

messages.content: Atlanta update: the organizers confirmed both Thursday and Friday morning roundtables start at 8:00 at the Hyatt Regency. The block deadline is tomorrow. Is the Hampton savings still worth it?

That changes the lodging math in favor of the block.

| Hotel | Est. 2-night lodging total | 8:00 a.m. timing | Breakfast/room basics | Cancellation | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Hyatt Regency block | about $512 | elevator ride to roundtables | breakfast not included; coffee listed; mini-fridge should be confirmed | block says refundable with advance cancellation, exact timestamp to capture | best fit now |
| Hampton Downtown | about $372 | 8-10 min walk or short rideshare both mornings | breakfast included; coffee + mini-fridge listed | usually flexible until day before | cheaper, but adds morning friction |
| Residence Inn Downtown | about $419 | 10-12 min walk/MARTA area | breakfast included; kitchenette/fridge | usually flexible until day before | middle option, not as convenient |
If breakfast isn’t included at the Hyatt, are we giving up too much value?

Not too much for a two-night work trip. Hampton probably saves about $140 on lodging and gives you two breakfasts, but the early roundtables mean the Hyatt avoids two rushed mornings, weather risk, and possible rideshares. If reimbursement accepts the official block, the convenience is defensible.
Room basics: is there a standard one-bed room, and can we confirm coffee and a fridge? I don’t want a surprise there.

The block is showing a standard king as the cleanest one-bed option, with a standard queen-type room as fallback if the king disappears. In-room coffee is listed. The refrigerator language is the one to verify directly: add a request for a mini-fridge and call the hotel/block desk to confirm whether it is standard in that room type or request-only.
And dinner Wednesday?

Hyatt wins there too. You can use the on-site restaurant/bar or Peachtree Center options without repositioning after the reception. Hampton has workable nearby restaurants, but you’d still need to get back there afterward.
What cancellation terms should I watch?

For the Hyatt block, capture the exact cancellation deadline during booking; the block language appears to be refundable with advance cancellation, likely around 72 hours before arrival, but the timestamp matters. Hampton and Residence Inn are more likely to allow cancellation closer to arrival, often the evening before. Avoid prepaid/nonrefundable versions for all of them.
So your recommendation is Hyatt now?

Yes. With 8:00 a.m. roundtables inside the Hyatt, I’d hold the refundable Hyatt block before the deadline. The Hampton savings are real, but not large enough to justify two early transfers unless reimbursement rejects the block rate.
Okay, hold Hyatt block. Standard king; queen is fine if that’s the only refundable one-bed. Quiet non-smoking, no prepay. Please include itemized folio and ask about the fridge.

Use this booking note: Hyatt Regency Atlanta event block, Jan. 27-29, 1 adult, refundable block rate, standard king preferred; queen one-bed acceptable if it is the flexible option. Requests: quiet non-smoking room, confirm in-room coffee maker, confirm or request mini-fridge, no prepaid/nonrefundable rate, itemized folio at checkout, and record the exact cancellation deadline and confirmation number.
